# opencode-db-client

One package (not published yet) provides an OpenCode v1/v2 plugin and a standalone `dbcanvas` terminal app. The plugin TUI registers a fullscreen page (`/db`) combining a live ER canvas (draggable tables, multi-select, FK arrows, schema sidebar) with a live schema browser: configure `connections` in the plugin options and the sidebar shows live databases → tables, with a read-only paginated browse strip. Connection profiles carry only an **env var name** — secrets resolve from `process.env` at connect time and never appear in config, logs, toasts, or snapshots. Query mode (`q`) adds a read-only SQL editor with a results grid, FK Jump into the browse strip, cancel/timeout/row caps, and narrow-terminal single-pane tabs (all values below are fake examples). Agent-side DB tools (`db_connect`, `db_list_tables`, `db_describe_table`, `db_records`, `db_query` with a server-side read-only guard) share the same `src/server/db/` core (profiles without secrets, redacted URL helpers, per-location pool registry over `bun:sqlite`/`Bun.SQL`).

## What is set up

- Separate prebuilt `./server` and `./tui` exports. Each module has one default object containing the v1 (`server` or `tui`) and v2 (`setup`) loader contracts.
- OpenCode v1 TUI route/keymap and v2 plugin-page/slot-keymap adapters; one host-neutral draggable-box canvas probe with keyboard fallback.
- A small diagnostic server tool registered via v1 `Hooks.tool` or v2 `tool.transform`.
- Bun build and tests, CI, npm packaging and tag-triggered OIDC publish workflow.

## Development

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run typecheck
bun run test
bun run build
npm pack --dry-run
```

The bundle must be rebuilt after source changes. Restart a running OpenCode host to load the new bundle. OpenCode v1 **and** v2 were targeted using the respective public plugin types; see [the compatibility plan](docs/setup-and-compatibility.md) for the tested versions and remaining runtime verification.

For the timestamped analysis of the reference video and the proposed database-client milestones, see [DB client canvas/TUI plan](docs/db-client-plan.md).

### Test this local playground

The checked-in `opencode.jsonc` and `tui.jsonc` load this checkout as a `file:` plugin **when OpenCode is launched from this repo**. Run `bun install && bun run build`, restart OpenCode, and launch `opencode2 .` (v2) or `opencode .` (v1) here. Open `/db` from slash completion or find **DB Client: Open Canvas** in the command palette; `<leader>d` is also registered. Without any connection the page shows an empty state (`no database connected · press a to add a connection`); there is no built-in demo schema.

### Adding a connection (in the TUI, no config edit needed)

Press `a` (or click **+ add connection**) anywhere on the `/db` page. Fill name, provider (`sqlite`/`postgres`/`mysql`, cycle with ←/→ or space), and:
- **sqlite:** file path (or `:memory:`) — no secret needed.
- **postgres/mysql:** host, port, database, user, plus the **name** of an env var holding the password **or full URI**. A URI such as `postgres://app:…@db.example/app?sslmode=disable` retains its query parameters when supplied through that env var.

Alternatively, enter a name and paste a **full URI** in the last form field for a **one-time connection**. The field masks the URI, never persists it, and passes it directly to the DB client in memory; disconnecting forgets the profile. For connections you want to reuse, put the URI in an environment variable and enter only that variable's name.

`Enter` moves between fields and submits from the last one; `Esc` cancels. Saving writes only the profile (env var **names**, never values) to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode-db-client/connections.json` and connects immediately. `c` toggles connect/disconnect, `✎` beside a saved connection opens its **prefilled edit form**, and `✕` deletes it. Profiles from plugin config (`connections` array) merge in automatically; edit those in config. One-time URI connections cannot be edited or reconnected after disconnect — paste again instead.

Example config entries (fake values only):

```jsonc
{ "plugin": [["file:/Users/duytrinh/Code/opencode-db-client", {
  "connections": [
    { "name": "shop", "provider": "sqlite", "database": "/tmp/shop.db" },
    { "name": "warehouse", "provider": "postgres", "host": "127.0.0.1",
      "port": 5432, "database": "app", "user": "app", "envVar": "SHOP_DB_PASSWORD" },
  ],
}]] }
```

### Query editor

Once connected, press `q` (or click the **[Query]** tab) to open the SQL editor. Type multi-line SQL (`Enter` for newline), run with `Ctrl+Enter` or the **[ run ]** button; `Esc` cancels a running query. Only single-statement read-only `SELECT`/`WITH`/`EXPLAIN` queries execute — writes and stacked statements are rejected before touching the database. `Tab` cycles sidebar → editor → results, arrows move the result cell, `Enter` on an FK cell jumps to the referenced table. Every FK relationship is always shown as a thin one-cell glyph connector (`●`, `─`, `│`, `┌┐└┘`, `<`/`>`) anchored to the actual FK/PK rows, grid-routed around table boxes and never through them. Selection only highlights table borders and drives the footer — it never hides relationships. Drag any table with the left mouse button; drag a rectangle on empty canvas for marquee multi-select, click selects, shift-click multi-selects, arrows move the selection, `enter` selects from the sidebar, `r` resets the layout, `esc` clears the selection then exits. Pan the viewport with `Ctrl+arrows` or the mouse wheel when tables overflow the visible area. The `mouse down`/`drag` counters show whether mouse events reached the page. When disconnected, the canvas shows an empty state; once connected, it shows the live schema (with a `loading tables ⠋ n/N` progress line while tables are introspected). If `/db` does not appear, inspect the resolved plugin config and host logs first.

The local config uses this machine's absolute path. If you relocate the checkout, update both files. No database credentials are needed to open the page; the canvas stays empty until you connect. The reference video is excluded from Git.

### Connect a database (env var only, values stay out of config)

Pass `connections` on the plugin entry as a tuple (all values below are fake examples). Each profile carries an env var **name**; the password or DSN is read from `process.env` at connect time. The TUI always connects read-only.

```jsonc
{
  // In tui.jsonc (and the same shape works in opencode.jsonc for agent tools):
  "plugin": [["file:/Users/duytrinh/Code/opencode-db-client", {
    "connections": [
      { "name": "local-sqlite", "provider": "sqlite", "database": ":memory:" },
      { "name": "local-pg", "provider": "postgres", "host": "localhost", "database": "FAKE_DB", "user": "FAKE_USER", "envVar": "FAKE_PG_DSN" }
    ]
  }]]
}
```

```sh
# Fake example only — point this at your real DSN or password outside the repo:
export FAKE_PG_DSN="postgres://FAKE_USER:FAKE_PASS@localhost:5432/FAKE_DB"
```

With connections configured, `/db` shows a `conn · …` bar (`c` connects/disconnects), a connections list with status dots, and — once connected — live databases → tables with `/` search, loading/error/empty/retry states, a column inspector, and a read-only paginated browse strip (`n`/`p` pages). The canvas shows **live ER nodes** derived from the real schema (tables with actual columns/PK/FK, edges from live foreign keys; capped at 30 tables with a header notice — a sidebar-driven "add table to canvas" for larger schemas is a follow-up). All drag/select/marquee/edge interactions work identically on live nodes, node positions persist per connection+database (positions only, never credentials) under `$XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode-db-client/layouts.json`, and disconnect returns the canvas to its empty state. Press `q` for Query mode: a multi-line SQL editor (`Enter` newline, `Ctrl+Enter` run, editor keystrokes never trigger canvas hotkeys) with a read-only results grid (sticky header, row numbers, `NULL`/bool/timestamp display, truncated cells with `…`, returned-vs-truncated counts, elapsed time, cancel via `Esc`, error with retry). `Tab` cycles sidebar → editor → results; `Esc` closes the `?` help overlay first, then cancels a running query, then clears selection. From a focused result cell on an FK column, `Enter` jumps to the referenced table in the browse strip filtered by that value (`x` clears the filter). Terminals narrower than 80 columns fall back to single-pane tabs. Without connections the page shows the empty state with an add-connection hint. Writes are blocked (guard rejects DML/DDL/multi-statement before any DB hit).

### Local installation elsewhere (unpublished package)

Build first, then point your config at this directory using a `file:` spec, **not a bare absolute path**. For OpenCode v1, add the server entry to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{ "plugin": ["file:/Users/duytrinh/Code/opencode-db-client"] }
```

Add the TUI entry to `~/.config/opencode/tui.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{ "plugin": ["file:/Users/duytrinh/Code/opencode-db-client"] }
```

Merge into existing arrays rather than replacing your other plugins. v2 can load the same `file:` package spec from its `plugins` configuration (and migrates v1-style `plugin` entries). It resolves the `./server` and `./tui` package exports. In the TUI, invoke `/db`, choose **DB Client: Open Canvas** from the palette, or press `<leader>d` (configurable through `{ "openKey": "..." }` on the plugin entry; use a lowercase key name — an uppercase one may be rejected by the host keymap parser).

After publication, substitute `@bojackduy/opencode-db-client` for the `file:` spec in the same configuration. The name is **not published yet**.

### Publishing

The single artifact (`@bojackduy/opencode-db-client@0.1.0`) is prepared for a scoped public npm release but is **not published**. The first publish must be done once by the package owner with npm authentication; the package needs to exist before npm can attach a trusted publisher:

```sh
npm login
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run prepack
npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts
npm publish --access public --provenance=false
```

Then on npmjs.com, configure the package's **Trusted Publisher → GitHub Actions** with owner `bojackduy`, repository `opencode-db-client`, workflow filename `npm-publish.yml` (no environment unless the workflow gains one). For subsequent releases, bump the version (starting with `0.1.1`), add its `## 0.1.1 (...)` CHANGELOG heading **before** tagging, then push `v0.1.1` (and repeat for later versions). `.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml` also supports manual dispatch **on a tag only**: it rejects a branch, verifies the tag matches `package.json`, the changelog heading exists and the version is absent on npm, then builds/tests, verifies all three packed entrypoints, publishes with OIDC/provenance and creates a GitHub release using that version's notes. No `NPM_TOKEN` is needed. Do **not** push the initial tag until after that one-time manual publish and trusted-publisher setup; an already-published version is deliberately rejected by CI.

The repository has no GitHub remote; workflows only run after it is pushed to the intended repository. See [setup and compatibility](docs/setup-and-compatibility.md) for the design decisions and next milestone.

## Two ways to run it — one package

`@bojackduy/opencode-db-client` ships both products from the same tarball: the OpenCode plugin (`dist/server.js` + `dist/tui.js`) and a standalone terminal app (`dist/dbcanvas.js`, exposed as the `dbcanvas` bin). Both mount the same canvas, SQL editor, and read-only DB core; the UI only talks to a small `DbHost` interface (`src/tui/host.ts`) with three adapters — OpenCode v1, OpenCode v2, and standalone.

**Inside OpenCode** — after publication, add the package to your config (v2 reads one `plugins` entry for server + TUI; v1 needs the same package in both `opencode.json` for the server and `tui.json` for the TUI):

```jsonc
// opencode.json (v1 server) and tui.json (v1 TUI)
{ "plugin": ["@bojackduy/opencode-db-client"] }
// v2 uses { "plugins": ["@bojackduy/opencode-db-client"] }
```

**As a normal app**, after publication (needs Bun; npm 7+ installs the OpenTUI/Solid peers):

```sh
npm i -g @bojackduy/opencode-db-client   # or: bun add -g @bojackduy/opencode-db-client
dbcanvas            # --help, --version
```

From a checkout: `bun run standalone` (source) or `bun run build && ./dist/dbcanvas.js`.

The app starts with the empty state; `a` adds a connection (fields + env-var secret, or a one-time pasted URI). Saved connections are the same secrets-free file the plugin uses (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode-db-client/connections.json`), so they show up in both. `Esc` (nothing selected) or `Ctrl+C` quits.

Why this works as one package: OpenTUI/Solid stay **peer** dependencies and every bundle keeps them external. Inside OpenCode the host provides its runtime; for the app, the package manager installs the peers alongside the package. Peers are `*` so OpenCode plugin installs do not fail on a host-version conflict; standalone compatibility with future OpenTUI versions will need ongoing testing.

# Changelog

## 0.1.0 (2026-09-29) — First npm release

### Standalone app, same package

- One package, two products: the tarball now ships the OpenCode plugin **and** a standalone `dbcanvas` terminal app (`bin` → `dist/dbcanvas.js`, `#!/usr/bin/env bun`). `bun run build` produces all three bundles; `bun run standalone` runs the app from source. A third `DbHost` adapter (`src/tui/adapters/standalone.ts`: fixed dark palette, in-app toast overlay, Esc/Ctrl+C quit) mounts the unchanged `CanvasPage` via OpenTUI `render()`; the app bundle has no `@opencode*` imports and shares saved connections with the plugin.
- OpenTUI/Solid remain peer dependencies (external in every bundle), so the plugin keeps sharing the host runtime while `npm i -g` / `bun add -g` auto-install them for the app. Verified end to end: `npm pack` → `npm install -g` into a scratch prefix → the linked `dbcanvas` rendered the empty-state canvas in a real PTY with npm-resolved `@opentui/core@0.5.12` (+ darwin-arm64 native), `@opentui/solid@0.5.12`, `solid-js@1.9.12`.

### Empty state + honest loading

- Removed the built-in fixture schema (`users`/`orders`/`order_items`/`products`) from the shipped plugin. Disconnected, the canvas shows `no database connected` with an add/connect hint; the demo tables now live only in `test/fixture-schema.ts` and reach the page through a test-only `preview` prop.
- Fixed "no tables in this schema" appearing while a remote schema was still loading: each canvas load (connect, database switch, retry) now resets to a real loading state instead of reusing the previous load's "loaded" flag, and the canvas/header show `loading tables ⠋ n/N` progress. The empty message names the database (`no tables in reply2lead_prod`) and only appears once loading finished with zero tables.
- Live introspection runs 6 tables in parallel on postgres/mysql (pooled Bun SQL) instead of strictly one round-trip at a time; sqlite stays sequential. Table order on the canvas is unchanged. Table list and active database now update in one batch so the loader never introspects new tables against the previous database.

### Connect picks the profile database

- Connecting to postgres/mysql now browses the profile's own `database` when the server lists it, instead of the first catalog entry. Previously one-time URI connects to a non-alphabetical database (e.g. `template1` while `postgres` sorts first) showed a live sidebar with database rows but an empty canvas (`no tables in this schema`), because introspection ran against the wrong catalog. `pickInitialDatabase()` (tested) prefers the profile database and falls back to the first listed entry; sqlite is unaffected (`main`).

### Canvas load resilience

- Live canvas introspection is now per-table fault-isolated: one failing table (permissions, exotic types, transient errors) is skipped and counted instead of nuking the whole canvas into a silent empty state. Zero loaded tables with failures shows an error with a retry button; partial loads note the failed count in the header.

### Loading feedback

- Clicking a database no longer shows a silent empty canvas while tables load: the canvas shows an animated `loading tables ⠋…` indicator, the header carries it during reloads with stale nodes, and the sidebar loading line animates too. The spinner runs on a timer only while loading, so a frozen spinner also signals a stuck load.

### Readable tables + interactive browse

- Table nodes align column types in a column (names padded per table) and size to their content (24–44 cells); overlong rows truncate with `…` instead of spilling. The footer is now short segmented hints with highlighted keys plus a colored selection count.
- The browse strip is interactive: `j`/`k` scroll rows, `,`/`.` shift the column window (`cols a-b/N` in the title), `n`/`p` still page. (`n` correctly does nothing when the page already holds all rows — the rows were clipped, not missing.)

### Canvas pan

- The canvas viewport pans: `Ctrl+arrows` and the mouse wheel move the camera over content larger than the visible stage, clamped to the content bounds (plain arrows still move the selection). Node drag, rubber-band, edges, and layout persistence all operate in world coordinates.

### Crash fix + one-time URI connect

- Fixed the `TextBuffer is destroyed` TUI crash: every conditional branch on the canvas page now mounts fresh nodes per toggle (plain ternaries) instead of re-inserting shared static elements through `<Show>`. OpenTUI destroys unmounted nodes while parent-owned effects keep firing, so the old pattern ran `fg` updates on dead buffers — exactly the reported stack (`dist/tui.js` fixture-row effect). Added `test/branch-toggle.test.ts` locking sidebar and browse/query toggle behavior.
- Added one-time full-URI connect: paste `postgres://…?sslmode=disable` (or any provider URI) into the connection form's last field to connect without saving anything. The URI travels only through the connect call, is masked in the form, and is forgotten on disconnect. The `envVar` field also accepts a variable holding a complete DSN URI with query parameters intact.
- TUI layout containment (from the overlap screenshots): clipped canvas viewport, independently scrolling sidebar, bounded browse panel with truncated labels, and Query mode owning the main pane instead of rendering over the canvas. Plugin surfaces stay opaque under translucent host themes.

- Give the canvas a clipped viewport and the sidebar its own scroll area; bound the browse metadata/rows panel and truncate long labels so dense schemas cannot paint across pane borders.
- Query mode now owns the main pane instead of rendering over the ER canvas. Its editor and results have bounded heights, an always-visible Run/Retry control, and clipped scrollable rows. Plugin page backgrounds are rendered opaque even when the host theme uses translucent surfaces.

### Goal 6 — live ER canvas + layout persistence + polish

- Added `src/tui/live-canvas.ts`: pure `buildLiveCanvas()` mapping live introspection rows to canvas nodes (`TableDef` with real columns/PK/FK) + FK edges, plus async `loadLiveCanvas()` over the store's live connection (read-only catalog/`PRAGMA` introspection only, sequential per-table fetches so single-connection drivers never see concurrent queries). The initial live canvas is capped at `LIVE_CANVAS_MAX_TABLES = 30` tables (header shows `live · N tables (showing S of T; cap 30)` when truncated; edges to off-canvas tables are dropped); a sidebar-driven "add table to canvas" for oversized schemas is a documented follow-up.
- Added `src/tui/layout.ts`: secrets-free layout persistence — positions only, keyed by `connectionId/database` (table ids are schema-qualified exactly when the canvas qualifies them), stored best-effort at `$XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode-db-client/layouts.json` (override via `DB_CLIENT_STATE_DIR`, used by tests); load on connect, save on drag end / arrow move / reset; every failure is silent with fixture fallback. Never credentials, never query text.
- Rewired `CanvasPage` onto `displayTables()`/`displayEdges()`: when connected, live nodes render with real columns/PK/FK markers and live FK arrows, keeping every interaction (group drag, click/shift-click, rubber-band marquee, arrows, `r` reset, `esc`) working on live nodes; disconnected restores the exact fixture playground. Added `?` help overlay listing the real bindings (Esc closes it first), per-mode footer hints (Browse vs Query), an empty-canvas state (`no tables in this schema`), and a live header replacing the fixture label. All new UI reads only `DbTheme` (no hardcoded colors); narrow-terminal single-pane behavior unchanged.
- Added `test/tui-canvas-live.test.ts` (4 tests: live sqlite schema → nodes render + drag works + drag-end persists positions secrets-free + disconnect restores fixture; layout roundtrip incl. corrupt-JSON fallback; help overlay open/Esc-close; pure mapping + cap enforcement with off-canvas edges dropped). Updated `test/tui-browser.test.ts` for the forced behavior change (live nodes replace fixture nodes while connected). Full suite now 103 pass / 4 skip (pg/mysql live) / 0 fail.
- Verified `dist/tui.js` still pulls only shared pure modules (query guard policy, schema introspection, pool client) — no agent tools (`createTools`/`db_query`), no server-only imports; the single `Bun.SQL` match is the bundler `// @bun` pragma comment.
- Added `docs/SECURITY.md` (secret handling, read-only default, caps/timeouts, guard policy, no history persistence checklist); updated README (live canvas + layout + help) and `docs/db-client-plan.md` with the Goal 6 final status.

### Goal 5 — TUI SQL editor + results grid

- Added `src/tui/query.ts`: `createQueryStore()` running read-only SQL in-process over the same db core path as the agent `db_query` tool (`validateReadOnlyQuery` pre-check → results cleared immediately on execute → `DbClient.query` with AbortSignal timeout + maxRows cap → `{columns,rows,rowCount,truncated,elapsedMs}`; `cancel()` aborts in-flight; superseded runs dropped by generation guard; history in-memory only, errors redacted, no secrets stored).
- Added pure, tested helpers: `formatResultCell` (`NULL`/bool/`Date`-as-ISO/JSON), `truncateCell` (visible `…` indicator), `resolveFkJump` + `quoteLiteral`/`buildFkWhere` (FK Jump filter builder), `nextEscAction` (cancel-query → clear-rubber → clear-selection → back), `classifyEditorKey` (only Ctrl/Cmd+Enter runs, Tab cycles, Esc; every canvas hotkey is plain editor input).
- Extended `src/tui/data.ts` with an optional browse `where` filter (`selectTable(sel, { where })`, `clearBrowseFilter`, threaded through `getRecords`) plus exported `browseDatabaseFor`/`browseRefFor` (sqlite `main` rule, postgres `schema.table` refs); all prior call sites behave exactly as before when no filter is set.
- Wired `CanvasPage`: Query mode (`q`) alongside Browse — multi-line textarea (`Enter` newline per OpenTUI defaults, `Ctrl+Enter` runs, text read via ref `plainText`, editor focus suppresses all global canvas hotkeys), Run/Cancel affordance, results grid (sticky header, row numbers, cell cursor, horizontal+vertical scroll via scrollbox capped at 100 rendered rows, footer with returned-vs-truncated counts + elapsed + cancel state + error with click-retry), `Tab` cycles sidebar → editor → results, FK Jump (`Enter` on a result cell resolves the Browse-selected table's FKs and opens the referenced table filtered by that value; `x` clears the filter), and narrow terminals (<80 cols) fall back to single-pane tabs. Dual v1/v2 export, DbHost boundary, and canvas drag/select/rubber-band/edges behavior unchanged.
- Added `test/tui-query.test.ts` (15 tests: SELECT rows+counts, row-cap truncation, DML/DDL/multi-statement/locking rejection pre-execution with zero DB hits, immediate-clear + timeout + explicit cancel via a hanging client, NULL/truncation rendering, Esc priority, editor key isolation, FK helpers + browse filter roundtrip, narrow render with counts and guard-error footer); full suite now 99 pass / 4 skip (pg/mysql live) / 0 fail.

### Goal 4 — TUI data layer + live schema browser

- Added `src/shared/connections.ts`: `ConnectionProfileInput` + `parseConnections` (never throws; invalid entries dropped with a reason; secrets never accepted — envVar names only) and extended `parseOptions` with optional `connections: []` (defaults unchanged otherwise).
- Added `src/tui/data.ts`: `createDbStore()` over the server db core reused directly in the TUI process (same Bun runtime, no RPC bridge) — per-connection `idle/connecting/ready/error/disconnected` statuses, redacted errors, database/table caches, selected table + columns, paginated records state with in-flight cancel (AbortController + generation guard, stale rows stay visible during reload per lazysql), `nextPage`/`prevPage`/`retry`, read-only connects, and a `dispose` path. The TUI bundle pulls only pool/schema/urls/types (bun builtins); verified `dist/tui.js` contains no agent-tool or server-only imports.
- Wired `CanvasPage`: connection bar with status dot + `c` connect/disconnect, connections section above the schema tree, live databases → tables with `/` search filter and loading/error/empty/retry states, click-to-select loading a column inspector + read-only paginated browse strip (`n`/`p`). With no profiles configured the fixture sidebar/canvas render exactly as before (existing render test passes unmodified).
- Wired `plugin.tsx` (v1 + v2): each setup builds a store from `options.connections` and disposes it on cleanup.
- Added `test/tui-data.test.ts` (parseConnections validation, store connect/select/paginate against seeded sqlite file DBs, cancel-supersede, read-only enforcement, secrets never in state/errors) and `test/tui-browser.test.ts` (live sidebar + browse rows render, redacted error path); updated `parseOptions` assertions in `test/exports.test.ts` for the new `connections: []` default.

### Goal 3 — agent DB tools

- Added pure server-side query guard in `src/server/db/guard.ts` (re-exported from `db/index.ts`): `isSingleStatement` (conservative scanner aware of strings/identifiers/line/block comments/`$tag$` dollar quotes, single trailing `;` tolerated), `isReadOnlySelect` (allowlist SELECT/WITH…SELECT/VALUES/EXPLAIN-without-ANALYZE; rejects DML/DDL, data-modifying CTEs, `SELECT…INTO`, locking reads), `clampMaxRows`/`clampTimeoutMs`, and throwing `validateReadOnlyQuery`. `pg_sleep`-style functions stay allowed with statement/AbortSignal timeouts as the backstop.
- Extended `src/server/tools.ts` from 1 to 9 v1-shape tools (dual v1/v2 adaptation unchanged): `db_connect` (secretless profile, returns `{connectionId,provider,database,readOnly}`), `db_disconnect`, `db_test_connection` (ephemeral, no registry write), `db_list_databases`, `db_list_tables`, `db_describe_table` (columns/PK/outgoing FKs/incoming references/indexes), `db_records` (paginated, capped, `{columns,rows,hasMore}`), `db_query` (guard enforced server-side, host AbortSignal timeout, `{rows,rowCount,truncated,elapsedMs}`). All outputs JSON strings; all errors via `redactError`. Registries stay per-location. Note: `@opencode-ai/plugin@1.18.32` `tool()` has no permission field, so `db_query` requires explicit host-level user approval (documented in code + tool description); the guard is the enforcement boundary.
- Added `test/db-tools.test.ts`: sqlite `:memory:` end-to-end through `createTools('v1', dir)` (connect→seed→listTables→describe both FK directions→records→query→disconnect), `db_query` rejection of DML/DDL/multi-statement/stacked/comment-smuggling even on `readOnly:false` connections, invalid-identifier rejection, abort/cancel path, ephemeral `test_connection` + secret redaction, per-location isolation, and guard unit tests.
- Updated `test/exports.test.ts` for the 9-tool v2 registration contract; canvas playground untouched.

- Added read-only server-side schema introspection in `src/server/db/schema.ts` (re-exported from `index.ts`): `listDatabases`, `listTables` (grouped by schema) + `listTableRefs`, `getColumns`, `getPrimaryKeys`, `getForeignKeys`/`getReferencingTables` (both directions), `getIndexes`, `getViews`, `getEstimatedRowCount`/`getExactRowCount`, paginated `getRecords` (`{columns,rows,hasMore}` via fetch limit+1). Provider switch ports lazysql query shapes: postgres via information_schema + pg_catalog (`$n` params, `schema.table` required), mysql via information_schema + `SHOW` (backtick quoting, `?` params), sqlite via sqlite_master + `PRAGMA foreign_key_list/table_info/index_list` (reverse FKs resolved by per-table PRAGMA scan, no version-dependent pragma functions). Identifier validation + per-provider quoting on every path; WHERE must start with WHERE and ORDER BY is identifier-list-only; all queries go through `DbClient.query` so pool timeouts/row caps/read-only guards/redaction apply. No agent tools yet (Goal 3).
